name: Predict Future Sales - Kaggle Benchmark Standard (2015) - Pipeline Template
summary: Tabular time-series and store-sales forecasting solution template for Predict Future Sales and Rossmann-style retail demand tasks, modeled as a deterministic pipeline with time aggregation, holiday and calendar feature engineering, target clipping, lag and rolling-window aggregate generation, entity/shop/store/category embeddings or encodings, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, GBDT modeling, and downstream competition-specific finalization.
dejargonized_summary: This template captures ordered retail forecasting steps: aggregate transactions or store sales by time, add calendar, holiday, promotion, store, and product features, build lag and rolling-window demand statistics, encode store/day/category entities, train XGBoost or LightGBM with tuned hyperparameters, and convert outputs into the final benchmark submission.

inputs.name: raw_competition_data
inputs.constraints: Raw data for a Tabular Time Series Forecasting task.

outputs.name: solution_predictions
outputs.constraints: Final predictions formatted for the benchmark metric.

use_when: The new task has the same broad problem type: tabular time-series, retail sales, store sales, product demand, or grouped temporal forecasting.

The available data supports the same ordered transformations and intermediate artifacts as the documented winning pipeline, including store/shop/product/date groups, holidays, promotions, calendar fields, lag features, or rolling windows.
Offline processing is acceptable, including search, feature extraction, model ensembling, or post-processing stages.
do_not_use_when: The target task lacks the modality or metadata required by the early pipeline stages.
Strict real-time inference is required and the template depends on heavyweight extraction, search, ensembling, or test-time augmentation.
The evaluation metric rewards a fundamentally different output structure than the source competition.
applicability.key_insight: The load-bearing idea is the pipeline topology: time aggregation plus leakage-safe lag, rolling-window, calendar, holiday, promotion, and entity encodings create the representation needed by GBDT modeling, so later stages optimize the metric without solving raw-data routing from scratch.

swappable_stages.lag_feature_generation: Can use fixed lags, rolling-window aggregates, expanding means, recent demand statistics, or same-day/week/month offsets as long as future target leakage is excluded.
swappable_stages.mean_encoding: Can use store, shop, item, category, day-of-week, month, holiday, promotion, target encoding, or learned entity embeddings.
swappable_stages.gbdt_modeling: The final model, Bayesian hyperparameter search policy, or ensemble can often be replaced if it preserves the same input/output contract and metric semantics.

applicability.scaling_notes: Scale bottlenecks are usually in feature extraction, graph/retrieval stages, neural inference, solver loops, and ensemble evaluation; cache intermediate artifacts when adapting this CDG.
failure_modes: Distribution shift breaks handcrafted thresholds, validation-derived weights, or post-processing rules.
Missing metadata prevents faithful construction of candidates, groups, windows, graphs, or cross-validation folds.
A weak first-stage recall, search, or representation step cannot be fully recovered by downstream rescoring or ensembling.

planning_constraints.subject: preserve_stage_order
planning_constraints.statement: Pipeline stages must execute in the documented order unless a replacement stage preserves the same input/output artifact contract.
planning_constraints.rationale: Downstream stages assume artifacts produced by earlier transformations.

planning_constraints.subject: validation_leakage_guard
planning_constraints.statement: Splits, folds, time ordering, store/product groups, holiday periods, and rolling windows from the source task must be respected when adapting the template.
planning_constraints.rationale: Many winning pipelines depend on leakage-safe validation, temporal grouping, and target encodings that exclude future rows.
